question.problem: Expressed as a nonnegative integer smaller than $8,$ the additive inverse of $19$ modulo $8$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
The additive inverse of $19$ modulo $8$ is the integer $0\le x<8$ such that

$$
x+19≡0\,(\text{mod}\,8).
$$

First, we note that $19≡3\,(\text{mod}\,8):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}19 & ≡2\cdot 8+3 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡2\cdot 0+3 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡3 & \,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Also, note that $-3+3≡0,$ so $x≡-3\,(\text{mod}\,8).$ To write this in the required form, we use the following sequence of congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡-3 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡0-3 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡8-3 & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\  & ≡5 & \,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the additive inverse of the element $19$ modulo $8$ is $5.$

We can verify this result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}19+5≡24≡3\cdot 8≡0\,\,✓\,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** In general, the additive inverse of $a$ modulo $n$ is simply the residue of $-a$ modulo $n,$ i.e. $-a\,\text{mod}\,n.$
